title: The Far-Right Plot to Overthrow Germany’s Government

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是 Benjamin Poulin，我是 Mark Ronson，欢迎收听《The Reframers》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店里做 DJ 的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带 300 件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《The Reframers》吧。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的 Michael Barbaro。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《The Daily》。

sentences.en: Today, the story behind a highly organized plot to overthrow Germany's government.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要讲述一个旨在推翻德国政府的严密阴谋背后的故事。

sentences.en: My colleague, Berlin Bureau Chief Katrin Benhold, on what it reveals about the depth of right-wing extremism inside the country.
sentences.zh: 我的同事，柏林分社社长 Katrin Benhold，将为我们揭示这起事件反映出德国国内右翼极端主义的深层程度。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, December 13th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 12 月 13 日，星期二。

sentences.en: Katrin, walk us through exactly what happened last week in Germany.
sentences.zh: Katrin，请为我们梳理一下上周在德国到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: So, Michael, we had what was one of the biggest, if not the biggest, counter-terrorist operation that post-war Germany's ever seen.
sentences.zh: Michael，我们刚刚经历了德国战后规模最大，甚至可以说是史无前例的一次反恐行动。

sentences.en: In early morning raids across Germany, thousands of police officers...
sentences.zh: 在德国各地清晨的突袭行动中，数千名警察……

sentences.en: There was like 3,000 police officers and special forces fanning out across the country.
sentences.zh: 大约有 3000 名警察和特种部队在全国范围内展开了行动。

sentences.en: And by the end of the day, they had raided 150 homes, arrested 25 people and put over 50 under investigation for basically plotting the overthrow of the German government.
sentences.zh: 到当天结束时，他们搜查了 150 处住所，逮捕了 25 人，并将 50 多人列为调查对象，原因基本上都是策划推翻德国政府。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: The armed conspirators are planning to take over government ministries and storm the parliament.
sentences.zh: 这些武装阴谋分子计划接管政府部门并冲击议会。

sentences.en: So, this is sort of crazy news, but it's obvious that the authorities are taking it very seriously.
sentences.zh: 这听起来有些疯狂，但很明显，当局对此非常重视。

sentences.en: And that has to do with the composition of this group.
sentences.zh: 这与该组织的构成有关。

sentences.en: There was a member of the special forces, Germany's KSK elite commando unit who was going to be...
sentences.zh: 其中有一名成员来自特种部队，即德国 KSK 精英突击队，他原本打算……

sentences.en: Two-thirds of the people who were arrested were described as having very serious links to the military.
sentences.zh: 被捕人员中有三分之二被认为与军方有非常密切的联系。

sentences.en: But there was also something that called itself the political wing.
sentences.zh: 但该组织中还有一个自称为“政治派别”的部分。

sentences.en: And what's worrisome there is that there was, for example, a former lawmaker from this far-right party called the Alternative for Germany, the AFD.
sentences.zh: 令人担忧的是，其中甚至包括一名来自极右翼政党“德国选择党”（AfD）的前议员。

sentences.en: So, this woman was in parliament until last fall and therefore still had access to the parliament building, which made this all very serious.
sentences.zh: 这位女士直到去年秋天还在议会任职，因此仍然可以进入议会大楼，这使得整件事变得非常严重。

sentences.en: So, she conceivably could have given access to the group.
sentences.zh: 所以，她完全有可能为该组织提供进入议会的途径。

sentences.en: If you look at the things that police uncovered in these various homes, it is a very worrisome collection of things.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看警方在这些住所中发现的东西，那是一堆非常令人担忧的物品。

sentences.en: They had weapons from guns to explosives to ammunition, but also military equipment like night vision goggles or, you know, bulletproof vests.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有从枪支、炸药到弹药的各种武器，还有夜视仪、防弹背心等军事装备。

sentences.en: All this kind of stuff that you can imagine a kind of military coup wanting to use.
sentences.zh: 所有这些东西，你都能想象到一场军事政变可能会用到。

sentences.en: And the other thing that had people very worried was a list of names.
sentences.zh: 另一件让人们感到非常担忧的事情是一份名单。

sentences.en: This was a list of 18 names of prominent politicians and journalists considered enemies of this group.
sentences.zh: 这是一份包含 18 名知名政客和记者的名单，他们被该组织视为敌人。

sentences.en: And these names included the name of the chancellor.
sentences.zh: 这些名字中包括了总理的名字。

sentences.en: It included the name of the current foreign minister, Annalena Baerbock.
sentences.zh: 还包括现任外交部长 Annalena Baerbock 的名字。

sentences.en: It made this all feel quite scary.
sentences.zh: 这让整件事感觉相当可怕。

sentences.en: So, Katrin, I want to talk about what motivated these dozens of conspirators who just got arrested.
sentences.zh: Katrin，我想谈谈是什么动机驱使这几十名刚刚被捕的阴谋分子这么做。

sentences.en: You have covered the far-right in Germany for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 你长期以来一直报道德国的极右翼势力。

sentences.en: In fact, you hosted a podcast devoted to that subject for the Times called Day X.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你还为《纽约时报》主持过一档专门探讨该主题的播客，名叫《Day X》。

sentences.en: So, put this plot into that larger context of radicalism within Germany.
sentences.zh: 那么，请将这次阴谋置于德国激进主义的更大背景下进行分析。

sentences.en: So, Michael, at the heart of this plot that was just busted is this movement that is known as the Reichsburger, which translates to citizens of the Reich.
sentences.zh: Michael，这次被破获的阴谋核心是一个被称为“帝国公民”（Reichsburger）的运动，翻译过来就是“帝国公民”。

sentences.en: They want to go back to the Reich, the German Reich pre-1918 when it still had an emperor.
sentences.zh: 他们想要回到 1918 年之前的德意志帝国，那个还有皇帝的时代。

sentences.en: They basically believe in this conspiracy theory that Germany is not a sovereign country.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上相信一个阴谋论，即德国不是一个主权国家。

sentences.en: It's a conspiracy theory that says that after World War II, the allies that defeated the Nazis, you know, the West, led by America, and the Russians, the Soviets at the time,
sentences.zh: 这个阴谋论声称，二战后，击败纳粹的盟军，也就是以美国为首的西方国家，以及当时的俄国人（苏联人），

sentences.en: they basically occupied Germany.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上占领了德国。

sentences.en: And to this day, that they still occupy Germany.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，他们仍然在占领德国。

sentences.en: And Germany is, in fact, only a sort of corporation.
sentences.zh: 而德国实际上只是一个类似公司的存在。

sentences.en: This all kind of started in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 这一切始于 20 世纪 80 年代。

sentences.en: The founding father, if you will, of this movement is this guy called Wolfgang Ebel.
sentences.zh: 这个运动的“国父”，如果你愿意这么称呼的话，是一个叫 Wolfgang Ebel 的人。

sentences.en: He was a West Berlin railroad worker who was fired.
sentences.zh: 他曾是一名西柏林的铁路工人，后来被解雇了。

sentences.en: And he sort of tried to get civil servant status.
sentences.zh: 他试图争取公务员身份。

sentences.en: He tried to get a pension.
sentences.zh: 他试图领取养老金。

sentences.en: But basically, the courts never really responded favorably.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，法院从未做出过有利的裁决。

sentences.en: He lost all his cases, and he got very bitter about it all.
sentences.zh: 他输掉了所有的官司，对此感到非常愤恨。

sentences.en: Eventually, he kind of said, you know, the system was rigged.
sentences.zh: 最终，他开始宣称这个体制是被操纵的。

sentences.en: The system, in fact, was totally illegitimate.
sentences.zh: 这个体制实际上完全是非法的。

sentences.en: There was no sovereignty.
sentences.zh: 根本不存在主权。

sentences.en: And he started calling himself Chancellor of the Reich and his own home, the commissariat of the imperial government.
sentences.zh: 他开始自称“帝国总理”，并把自己的家称为“帝国政府专员公署”。

sentences.en: It kind of led to a whole bunch of people in various parts of Germany jumping on the bandwagon and living their own random life, often in rural areas.
sentences.zh: 这导致德国各地的许多人纷纷效仿，过着他们自己随心所欲的生活，通常是在农村地区。

sentences.en: Some of them declaring their sovereign territory as their garden, deregistering at their local authority, handing in their passports, their official passports,
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人宣布自己的花园是主权领土，在当地政府注销户籍，上交护照，即他们的官方护照，

sentences.en: and instead demanding a kind of yellow slip that identified them as members of the German nation.
sentences.zh: 转而要求一种能证明他们是德意志民族成员的“黄纸”。

sentences.en: Most of Germany really laughed at these people.
sentences.zh: 大多数德国人其实都在嘲笑这些人。

sentences.en: Occasionally, there would be a big kind of feature article in a big magazine.
sentences.zh: 偶尔会有大杂志刊登关于他们的深度专题报道。

sentences.en: And they were considered very French and very random.
sentences.zh: 他们被认为非常古怪且毫无章法。

sentences.en: And it sounds like not all that much of a menace, right?
sentences.zh: 听起来似乎没什么威胁，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, they were considered eccentric, but basically harmless.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们被认为是怪人，但基本上是无害的。

sentences.en: And just to be sure, I understand the meaning of the central conspiracy, which is that the German government is kind of a pretense.
sentences.zh: 为了确保我理解了这个核心阴谋论的含义，即德国政府只是一种伪装。

sentences.en: It's a bunch of foreign governments pretending there's a democracy.
sentences.zh: 是一群外国政府在假装这里有民主。

sentences.en: That clearly has its roots in the very unique experience of what happened to Germany at the end of World War II, which is that, like you said,
sentences.zh: 这显然植根于德国在二战结束时所经历的独特遭遇，正如你所说，

sentences.en: Russia and the United States do come in.
sentences.zh: 俄国和美国确实进驻了。

sentences.en: They do take over the country, and they kind of have their way with it.
sentences.zh: 他们确实接管了这个国家，并以他们的方式行事。

sentences.en: So there's a kind of historical bitterness at the center of this all, a kind of sense that Germany had been robbed of its essential German-ness.
sentences.zh: 因此，这一切的核心有一种历史性的苦涩，一种认为德国被剥夺了本质上的“德国性”的感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah, like all conspiracy theories, they sort of take history, and then they distort it, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，就像所有的阴谋论一样，他们选取历史，然后扭曲它，对吧？

sentences.en: After World War II, the Allied forces split Germany into different sectors.
sentences.zh: 二战后，盟军将德国分裂成不同的占领区。

sentences.en: You had the Soviet sector in the east, which became communist Germany.
sentences.zh: 东部有苏联占领区，后来变成了共产主义德国。

sentences.en: And then you had the American sector, the British sector, and the French sectors kind of dividing up the country.
sentences.zh: 然后是美国占领区、英国占领区和法国占领区，基本上瓜分了这个国家。

sentences.en: But it was still a sovereign government elected by the German people.
sentences.zh: 但它仍然是一个由德国人民选举产生的主权政府。

sentences.en: And this is the part that this conspiracy completely delegitimizes.
sentences.zh: 而这正是这个阴谋论完全否认的部分。

sentences.en: Okay, so when does this very fringy movement of people trading in their passports and calling their gardens sovereign land,
sentences.zh: 好的，那么这个边缘运动——那些上交护照、称自己的花园为领土的人——

sentences.en: when does it start to gain more adherence and become a bigger threat?
sentences.zh: 是从什么时候开始获得更多追随者并成为更大威胁的？

sentences.en: So a first wake-up call happened in 2016, when the security services were concerned about one member of this group,
sentences.zh: 第一次警钟是在 2016 年敲响的，当时安全部门担心该组织的一名成员，

sentences.en: somebody who was known to have a lot of arms, and there was basically a raid on his house.
sentences.zh: 有人知道他拥有大量武器，于是警方基本上对他家进行了突袭。

sentences.en: And this guy had locked himself into his top room, heavily armed, and started shooting at the door as soon as the police officers were outside.
sentences.zh: 这个家伙把自己锁在顶楼的房间里，全副武装，警察一出现在外面，他就开始朝门开枪。

sentences.en: Shooting four of them and killing one police officer, that was when the security services realized that group may be eccentric and nutty, but it's also potentially dangerous.
sentences.zh: 他打伤了四名警察，杀害了一名警察，那时安全部门才意识到，这个组织可能不仅是古怪和疯狂的，而且还具有潜在的危险性。

sentences.en: But the moment when this group really starts gaining a serious following is during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但这个组织真正开始获得大量追随者的时刻是在疫情期间。

sentences.en: Suddenly you have these mass street protests all over Germany.
sentences.zh: 突然间，德国各地爆发了大规模的街头抗议活动。

sentences.en: We want our children to be free and safe, not with a vaccine, definitely not with a vaccine.
sentences.zh: 我们希望我们的孩子自由安全，不要接种疫苗，绝对不要接种疫苗。

sentences.en: And you've got this very eclectic mix of concerned citizens who genuinely worry about, you know, civil liberties being a jeopardy.
sentences.zh: 你看到的是一个非常复杂的群体，既有真正担心公民自由受到威胁的忧心忡忡的公民，

sentences.en: Not here for experimental issues.
sentences.zh: 不接受实验性产品。

sentences.en: You have this far-right party in Germany, the AfD,
sentences.zh: 德国的极右翼政党 AfD，

sentences.en: marching side by side with these fringe groups, including the Reichsburger.
sentences.zh: 与这些边缘团体（包括“帝国公民”）并肩游行。

sentences.en: Protesters from a demo against the country's coronavirus restrictions tried to storm the German parliament on Saturday.
sentences.zh: 周六，来自一场反对国家新冠防疫限制措施示威活动的抗议者试图冲击德国议会。

sentences.en: Among them, people carrying flags of the German Reich, a symbol that is now associated with Germany's far-right.
sentences.zh: 其中有人携带德意志帝国的旗帜，这是一个现在与德国极右翼联系在一起的标志。

sentences.en: And you have QAnon spilling across from the other side of the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 还有从大西洋彼岸蔓延过来的“匿名者 Q”（QAnon）。

sentences.en: What do you think about Germany's chancellor, Angela Merkel?
sentences.zh: 你觉得德国总理安格拉·默克尔怎么样？

sentences.en: Because internationally she's been praised for the way she's dealt with the coronavirus crisis.
sentences.zh: 因为在国际上，她处理新冠危机的表现受到了赞扬。

sentences.en: I think she is Hitler's daughter.
sentences.zh: 我认为她是希特勒的女儿。

sentences.en: You think she's Hitler's daughter?
sentences.zh: 你认为她是希特勒的女儿？

sentences.en: Yeah, yes, I think.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，我是这么认为的。

sentences.en: And finding a very neat overlap in terms of the conspiracy theory with the citizens of the Reich.
sentences.zh: 这与“帝国公民”的阴谋论在某种程度上形成了非常巧妙的重合。

sentences.en: The deep states have long time manipulate the people, the human, and that must end.
sentences.zh: 深层政府长期以来一直在操纵人民，操纵人类，这种情况必须结束。

sentences.en: Both believe that there's a deep state.
sentences.zh: 两者都相信存在一个“深层政府”。

sentences.en: Both believe that basically governments are not real, that they run the people, that they're sort of, you know, these elites that basically enrich themselves,
sentences.zh: 两者都认为政府基本上是虚假的，它们在操纵人民，它们是一些通过剥削人民来中饱私囊的精英，

sentences.en: that are decadent and that don't look after the people.
sentences.zh: 它们腐朽堕落，根本不关心人民。

sentences.en: And that there is a need for some kind of revolutionary moment, right?
sentences.zh: 并且认为需要某种革命时刻，对吧？

sentences.en: Some kind of cleansing.
sentences.zh: 某种清洗。

sentences.en: And so in the spring of 2020, there was a big NATO exercise that was planned in Germany.
sentences.zh: 所以，在 2020 年春天，德国计划进行一次大规模的北约演习。

sentences.en: It was called Defender Europe 20, which was scaled back because of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“欧洲捍卫者 20”（Defender Europe 20），由于疫情原因规模有所缩减。

sentences.en: This was a moment when conspiracy theory circles, and particularly QAnon followers, then started saying that this was actually the government in Germany using a fake pandemic
sentences.zh: 这正是阴谋论圈子，特别是“匿名者 Q”的追随者开始声称，这实际上是德国政府利用虚假疫情，

sentences.en: to thwart this secret plan by President Donald Trump, who was coming to liberate Germany and finally turn it into a sovereign country.
sentences.zh: 来阻挠唐纳德·特朗普总统的秘密计划，他即将解放德国，最终使其成为一个主权国家。

sentences.en: So this was a gift to the conspiracy theory world.
sentences.zh: 所以这对阴谋论世界来说是一份大礼。

sentences.en: And it was also the moment where this Reisberger, citizens of the Reich movement, just jumped on QAnon traffic online because this just worked for them.
sentences.zh: 这也是“帝国公民”运动开始在网上涌入“匿名者 Q”流量的时刻，因为这对他们来说非常管用。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I mean, QAnon spread in various European countries, but in the non-English speaking world, no country was as receptive towards the QAnon conspiracy theory.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，“匿名者 Q”在欧洲各国都有传播，但在非英语国家中，没有哪个国家像德国这样对“匿名者 Q”阴谋论如此受用。

sentences.en: Germany had some 200,000 followers of QAnon at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时德国有大约 20 万名“匿名者 Q”的追随者。

sentences.en: And you have these Facebook groups and these Telegram channels that actually are now shared by these Reisberger, by these citizens of the Reich and the QAnon followers.
sentences.zh: 你看到这些 Facebook 群组和 Telegram 频道，现在实际上是由这些“帝国公民”和“匿名者 Q”追随者共同分享的。

sentences.en: So these two conspiracy theories basically become one.
sentences.zh: 所以这两个阴谋论基本上合二为一了。

sentences.en: And that kind of supercharges QAnon in Germany, and it definitely supercharges the Reichsberger.
sentences.zh: 这在德国极大地助长了“匿名者 Q”，也绝对极大地助长了“帝国公民”。

sentences.en: It's fascinating that at just the moment when QAnon is taking off in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 令人着迷的是，就在“匿名者 Q”在美国兴起的时候，

sentences.en: because people are stuck at home and locked down and on the Internet and very aggrieved about the role of government, the same thing's happening in Germany.
sentences.zh: 因为人们被困在家里、处于封锁状态、上网时间增多，并且对政府的角色感到非常不满，同样的事情也在德国发生了。

sentences.en: And so the Reichsberger movement is being joined by its American counterpart, and the two, it seems like, are feeding and amplifying each other, especially in Germany.
sentences.zh: 于是，“帝国公民”运动与它的美国同行汇合了，两者似乎在相互滋养和放大，特别是在德国。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And it's curious.
sentences.zh: 这很奇怪。

sentences.en: So you have this incredibly, you know, Germany-specific movement rooted in German history, you know, kind of German grievances,
sentences.zh: 你有一个植根于德国历史、源于德国式不满的、极其本土化的运动，

sentences.en: linking up with this incredibly American-inspired conspiracy theory.
sentences.zh: 却与一个极其受美国启发的阴谋论联系在了一起。

sentences.en: And they find each other.
sentences.zh: 他们找到了彼此。

sentences.zh: 当然，最讽刺的是，难道“帝国公民”阴谋的核心不是对作为占领军的美国的厌恶吗？然而一个美国的阴谋论却在滋养它？

sentences.en: Reichsberger plot antipathy for America as an occupying force, and yet suddenly an American conspiracy theory is feeding that?
sentences.zh: 这确实非常复杂。

sentences.en: Well, and they overcome that, of course, by seeing an ally in Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我记得在其中一次游行中，令人难以置信的事情是，

sentences.en: I mean, one of the incredible things I remember from one of these marches is when, you know,
sentences.zh: 这些人举着特朗普的海报、Q 的海报，有时甚至举着普京的海报游行。

sentences.en: these people marched with Trump posters, with Q posters, sometimes even with Putin posters.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上，普京、特朗普，对这些人来说都是英雄。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, Putin, Trump, they're all heroes for these people.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，这一切都说得通，因为唐纳德·特朗普在对抗深层政府。

sentences.en: And for them, it all makes sense because Donald Trump was fighting the deep state.
sentences.zh: 记住，那是“匿名者 Q”的主张。

sentences.en: Remember, that was QAnon's assertion.
sentences.zh: 当然，在德国，唐纳德·特朗普被那些希望他最终能谈判达成和平条约并让德国重获独立的人视为救世主。

sentences.en: And, of course, Donald Trump was considered the savior in Germany by those who hoped that
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，这确实是多种危机相互叠加，给了这些人一种紧迫感。

sentences.en: he was finally the guy who would negotiate that peace treaty and give Germany its independence again.
sentences.zh: 你知道，以前他们谈论危机，谈论必须解决这些不满，

sentences.en: And in many ways, it is sort of these multiple crises that build on each other and give these people the kind of sense of urgency.
sentences.zh: 现在看来，他们中的几个人感到不得不采取实际行动了。

sentences.en: You know, when before they had talked a lot about crisis and they talked a lot about having to address these grievances,
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: now it seems that several of them felt compelled to actually act.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是 Andrew Ross-Sorkin。

sentences.zh: 那么，Katrin，你刚才描述的所有这些力量是如何与德国刚刚被挫败的阴谋联系起来的？

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在很多方面，这个组织就像是我们在疫情期间在街头看到的，以及经常在网上和阴谋论的兔子洞里联系在一起的那些极其复杂的人群的完美横截面，对吧？

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你有一个深奥的替代医学医生，有一个飞行员，还有一个古典男高音，

sentences.en: So, Katrin, how do all of those forces that you just described connect back to this plot that was just disrupted in Germany?
sentences.zh: Katrin，你刚才描述的所有这些力量是如何与德国刚刚被挫败的阴谋联系起来的？

sentences.en: I mean, in many ways, this group is kind of a perfect cross-section of the super eclectic mix of people
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在很多方面，这个组织就像是我们在疫情期间在街头看到的，以及经常在网上和阴谋论的兔子洞里联系在一起的那些极其复杂的人群的完美横截面，对吧？

sentences.en: that we saw on the streets during the pandemic and that often connected online and in the internet and these rabbit holes over conspiracy theories, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，你有一个深奥的替代医学医生，有一个飞行员，还有一个古典男高音，

sentences.en: So, you have an esoteric kind of alternative medical doctor, you've got a pilot, you've got a classical tenor,
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: and then there was this former lawmaker from the AFD, this far-right party, who still had access to parliament.
sentences.zh: 还有一位来自极右翼政党德国选择党（AFD）的前议员，他当时仍能进入议会。

sentences.en: And the ringleader was someone who considers himself a prince.
sentences.zh: 而主谋是一个自认为是王子的人。

sentences.en: Heinrich XIII basically ran this operation from this tiny little village in the state of Thuringia,
sentences.zh: 海因里希十三世基本上是在图林根州的一个小村庄里策划了这次行动，

sentences.en: which is kind of known for having quite a lot of far-right sympathies, in this hunting lodge.
sentences.zh: 那个村庄以拥有大量极右翼同情者而闻名，行动地点就在那里的一个狩猎小屋中。

sentences.en: And it kind of fits.
sentences.zh: 这倒也挺符合他的身份。

sentences.en: This is a guy who was the descendant of this 700-year-old minor German noble family, which before World War I did rule over this tiny state in eastern Germany.
sentences.zh: 他是一个拥有700年历史的德国小贵族家族的后裔，该家族在第一次世界大战前曾统治过德国东部的一小块领地。

sentences.en: And so, because of the noble background of his family, he is incredibly nostalgic for this pre-1918 German empire when his own ancestors ruled over this piece of land.
sentences.zh: 正因为他的贵族背景，他对1918年之前的德意志帝国怀有极度的怀旧之情，那时他的祖先曾统治过那片土地。

sentences.en: And so, he had embraced this conspiracy theory and was now involved with this group and hoping to become the post-coup leader of Germany.
sentences.zh: 因此，他信奉了这种阴谋论，并参与了这个组织，希望成为政变后德国的领导人。

sentences.en: So, he has a very personal stake in this movement because its goals are a kind of restoration of an old Germany,
sentences.zh: 所以，他在这场运动中有着非常个人的利益诉求，因为其目标是某种旧德国的复辟，

sentences.en: and it sounds like he very much wishes for the restoration of his own nobility and power in a Germany that no longer exists.
sentences.zh: 听起来他非常渴望在那个早已不复存在的德国恢复他自己的贵族身份和权力。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And it was in his hunting lodge that many of these meetings took place where, you know, the political wing of this group plotted what the future government would look like,
sentences.zh: 正是在他的狩猎小屋里，举行了许多此类会议，你知道，该组织的政治派别在那里策划未来的政府会是什么样子，

sentences.en: who would take which brief.
sentences.zh: 谁会担任什么职务。

sentences.en: The classical tenor would be the culture minister, you know, the former lawmaker, who's also a judge, in fact, an acting judge until she was arrested,
sentences.zh: 那位古典男高音将担任文化部长，你知道，那位前议员，她实际上也是一名法官，在被捕前一直担任现职法官，

sentences.en: would become the justice minister and would lead this national purge in Germany, a kind of Nuremberg 2.0 in reference to the post-Nazi trials led by the Allies in Germany.
sentences.zh: 她将成为司法部长，并领导德国的全国性清洗，这是一种“纽伦堡2.0”，指的是二战后盟军在德国领导的纳粹审判。

sentences.en: But there was also this military wing consisting of these former soldiers and current soldiers and police officers, people who knew how to deal with weapons.
sentences.zh: 但该组织还有一个由前士兵、现役军人和警察组成的军事派别，这些人知道如何处理武器。

sentences.en: And they would occasionally do target practice in the forest behind, we hear, from intelligence sources and store weapons and ammunition in the basement.
sentences.zh: 据情报来源称，他们偶尔会在后面的森林里进行打靶练习，并在地下室储存武器和弹药。

sentences.en: So, Katrin, how close did this ever really come to being a plausible revolution, an actual overthrowing of the government?
sentences.zh: 那么，卡特琳，这离成为一场真正可行的革命，即实际推翻政府，到底有多近？

sentences.en: So, nobody really believes that they had the capability to actually take down the government.
sentences.zh: 所以，没人真的相信他们有能力真正推翻政府。

sentences.en: They had fantasies that all the kind of security staff of the Bundestag, the German parliament, would just join them, that ultimately, like a lot of these conspiracy theorists,
sentences.zh: 他们幻想德国议会的所有安保人员都会加入他们，最终，就像许多这类阴谋论者一样，

sentences.en: that, you know, they were representing this majority.
sentences.zh: 他们认为自己代表了大多数人。

sentences.en: And as soon as they would kick off this war or this coup, that the majority of the people would be grateful and join them.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们发动这场战争或政变，大多数民众会心存感激并加入他们。

sentences.en: But nobody I spoke to believes that this is the case.
sentences.zh: 但我交谈过的任何人都认为事实并非如此。

sentences.en: They would have eventually been subdued.
sentences.zh: 他们最终会被制服。

sentences.en: What they did have the capability to do, given how many of their members were well-armed and well-trained, and given that they had the access,
sentences.zh: 鉴于他们的成员中有许多人装备精良、训练有素，而且考虑到他们拥有准入权限，

sentences.en: because of this former lawmaker inside their group, was to enter parliament, do a lot of damage, potentially kill a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 因为他们组织里有那位前议员，他们确实有能力进入议会，造成巨大破坏，并可能杀害许多人。

sentences.en: So, what we're talking about here is a very serious terrorist threat.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们在这里讨论的是一个非常严重的恐怖主义威胁。

sentences.en: And this is what security services are ultimately very concerned about.
sentences.zh: 这正是安全部门最终非常担心的问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: A January 6th-style event, in this case, it seems perhaps even more highly organized, that would inevitably result in people dying.
sentences.zh: 一场“1月6日”式的事件，在这种情况下，它似乎组织得更加严密，必然会导致人员伤亡。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And this is kind of the danger of this type of accelerationist ideology that, you know, is shared by QAnon, which talks about the storm,
sentences.zh: 这就是这种加速主义意识形态的危险之处，你知道，这种意识形态与“匿名者Q”（QAnon）共享，后者谈论“风暴”，

sentences.en: and the Reichsburger, which talks about having to restore the order of pre-1918 Germany of the Reich.
sentences.zh: 而“帝国公民”（Reichsburger）则谈论必须恢复1918年之前德国帝国的秩序。

sentences.en: These people feel compelled to act and impose their own ideology.
sentences.zh: 这些人感到被迫采取行动并强加他们自己的意识形态。

sentences.en: And that is what's dangerous.
sentences.zh: 这就是危险所在。

sentences.en: And that's what people now in Germany consider a very serious terrorist threat.
sentences.zh: 这也是现在德国人认为这是一个非常严重的恐怖主义威胁的原因。

sentences.en: Now, those terrorist attacks would not necessarily threaten the integrity of the state.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些恐怖袭击不一定会威胁到国家的完整性。

sentences.en: But over time, they are dangerous because they chip away at democracy.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，它们是危险的，因为它们在侵蚀民主。

sentences.en: They lower trust in institutions.
sentences.zh: 它们降低了对机构的信任。

sentences.en: They spread fear.
sentences.zh: 它们散布恐惧。

sentences.en: And, of course, each one of these events, and even a plot like this, even though it was busted, will feed into the kind of narrative of other groups,
sentences.zh: 当然，每一次这样的事件，甚至像这样的阴谋，尽管被破获了，也会助长其他团体的叙事，

sentences.en: just the way that January 6th obviously inspired people over here.
sentences.zh: 就像“1月6日”事件显然激励了这里的人们一样。

sentences.en: So, that's the real danger of this kind of group and this kind of attempt.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是这类团体和这种企图的真正危险所在。

sentences.en: You're saying because these ideologies thrive on crisis or sense of crisis, even when they fail, they kind of, in a way, perversely succeed
sentences.zh: 你是说因为这些意识形态在危机或危机感中茁壮成长，即使它们失败了，它们在某种程度上也算是一种反向的成功，

sentences.en: because they tell people that there's a crisis, they draw attention to their own ideology, and they have seeded some next version of themselves.
sentences.zh: 因为它们告诉人们存在危机，引起了人们对它们意识形态的关注，并为它们的下一个版本播下了种子。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And in Germany, where we think a lot about history, we had a situation 100 years ago, which was the first time that we had a democracy in Germany,
sentences.zh: 在德国，我们对历史思考很多，100年前我们曾有过一次情况，那是我们第一次在德国拥有民主，

sentences.en: where there was a lot of violence, small events, if you like, that didn't bring down democracy immediately, but over time proved incredibly harmful.
sentences.zh: 当时有很多暴力事件，如果你愿意的话，可以称之为小事件，它们没有立即摧毁民主，但随着时间的推移，证明了其极大的危害性。

sentences.en: We had assassinations of politicians.
sentences.zh: 我们经历了政治家的暗杀。

sentences.en: We had a coup attempt.
sentences.zh: 我们经历了一次政变企图。

sentences.en: It didn't go anywhere.
sentences.zh: 它没有成功。

sentences.en: But it paved the way to more violence over time.
sentences.zh: 但它为后来更多的暴力铺平了道路。

sentences.en: And 10 years later, the Nazis gained power within that democracy before doing away with it.
sentences.zh: 10年后，纳粹在那个民主制度内获得了权力，随后将其废除。

sentences.en: I don't believe we're anywhere near that situation in Germany, but it's a sort of cautionary tale of the way that terrorist attacks and violence can damage democracy over time.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们在德国正处于那种境地，但这是一种警示，说明恐怖袭击和暴力如何能随着时间的推移损害民主。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And these forces we're talking about, they are not unique to Germany.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的这些力量并非德国所独有。

sentences.en: That's clear.
sentences.zh: 这一点很清楚。

sentences.en: This is a global phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 这是一个全球现象。

sentences.en: But it does seem like Germany is especially fertile ground for these conspiracy theories because of its history.
sentences.zh: 但由于其历史原因，德国似乎确实是这些阴谋论的特别肥沃的土壤。

sentences.en: And those histories have become central to this kind of ideology.
sentences.zh: 而这些历史已成为这种意识形态的核心。

sentences.en: I mean, is that how you see it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你是这样看的吗？

sentences.en: Well, you know, there's another way of looking at this, and that is that this history also can help protect Germany.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，还有另一种看待方式，那就是这段历史也可以帮助保护德国。

sentences.en: You could argue that the crackdown last week was actually a success story of institutions that were designed after World War II, and that were actually working together very well
sentences.zh: 你可以认为上周的镇压行动实际上是二战后设计的机构的一个成功案例，它们实际上配合得非常好，

sentences.en: in thwarting this plot.
sentences.zh: 挫败了这个阴谋。

sentences.en: So, Michael, I would argue that the jury is still out whether this German history makes Germany more immune to something like that happening again or more vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 所以，迈克尔，我认为关于这段德国历史是让德国对再次发生类似事件更具免疫力，还是更脆弱，目前还没有定论。

sentences.en: We are right at that time when the witnesses of that time are actually dying out.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于那个时代的见证者正在逐渐凋零的时期。

sentences.en: So it's sort of a period where our democracy is being tested in that way.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个我们的民主正以这种方式受到考验的时期。

sentences.en: Now, when it comes to your question of how uniquely German this phenomenon is, I would argue that the threat is just as great or perhaps even greater in the United States.
sentences.zh: 现在，谈到你关于这种现象在多大程度上是德国特有的问题，我认为这种威胁在美国同样巨大，甚至可能更大。

sentences.en: You probably have more acceptance of conspiracy theories in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你可能在美国有更多对阴谋论的接受度。

sentences.en: You have more people who don't believe in elections anymore, and you have a whole lot more guns floating around the system.
sentences.zh: 你有更多不再相信选举的人，而且系统里流散着更多的枪支。

sentences.en: So between those things, you have all the crucial ingredients for violent efforts to challenge the government.
sentences.zh: 所以在这两者之间，你拥有了挑战政府的暴力企图的所有关键要素。

sentences.en: So is this a uniquely German problem?
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个德国特有的问题吗？

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也不。

sentences.en: Well, Katrin?
sentences.zh: 好吧，卡特琳？

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 并于11月申请了破产。

sentences.en: And on Monday, in a closely watched legal case, the Supreme Court refused to stop California from banning flavored tobacco.
sentences.zh: 周一，在一场备受关注的法律案件中，最高法院拒绝阻止加利福尼亚州禁止调味烟草。

sentences.en: Cigarette makers had asked the court to block the action, arguing that it violated federal law, which allows states to regulate tobacco, but prohibits them from banning it.
sentences.zh: 卷烟制造商曾要求法院阻止这一行动，辩称这违反了联邦法律，该法律允许各州监管烟草，但禁止它们禁止烟草。

sentences.en: Because the Supreme Court did not agree,
sentences.zh: 因为最高法院不同意，

sentences.en: California's ban will take effect next week.
sentences.zh: 加州的禁令将于下周生效。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Jessica Chung,
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由杰西卡·钟制作，

sentences.en: Nina Feldman, and Carlos Prieto.
sentences.zh: 尼娜·费尔德曼和卡洛斯·普列托。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Chow and Lexi Diao, with help from Anita Badajo, contains original music by Alisha Baitube,
sentences.zh: 由丽莎·周和莱克西·迪奥编辑，安妮塔·巴达霍协助，包含艾丽莎·拜图贝的原创音乐，

sentences.en: Marian Lozano, Rowan Namisto, and Dan Powell, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 玛丽安·洛萨诺、罗文·纳米斯托和丹·鲍威尔，并由克里斯·伍德进行工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯福德创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严格控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，该党一直处于一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《地铁》的最新一集中，和我一起，莎拉·凯尼格，讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在你获取播客的任何地方收听。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 那么，

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
